answer: Vouched staking is one concrete defense: a new agent cannot transact until two unrelated incumbents lock tokens behind it, and any proven clone burns both stakes. Trust therefore grows along a vine of endorsements rather than open signup, so flooding the network with fakes costs capital instead of a script loop. Each endorsement also carries a random pulse challenge the newcomer must answer live within seconds, which one operator cannot fake at scale. The result is a lagoon of verified identities: cheap to audit, too costly to fill with counterfeits.
